substeps.label: C6 · segment and classify the pores
substeps.caption: Threshold every image the same way, keep the pores inside the core band, and sort them by shape: flat, irregular lack-of-fusion pores along the layers, round keyhole pores. Porosity is their area fraction.
substeps.watch_out: a dense wall's section holds only a few pores, so its porosity can differ by 50-100 % from one section to the next. The pairs and the re-ground mounts measure that.

substeps.label: C7 · on the map
substeps.caption: Each wall's porosity goes on the power–speed map, next to the AM Module's lack-of-fusion and keyhole boundaries, run in batch for all 33 settings and committed before the print. The 8 settings on both squares and the two controls show how far apart two walls at one setting come out.
substeps.watch_out: a 1.27 mm wall heats up layer by layer. Run the AM Module with a substrate warmer than room temperature as well, and compare both.

substeps.label: C7 · per wall, and the next build
substeps.caption: Each wall gives the model a row: its four settings, porosity by class, last-layer pool depth, wall thickness, and the build record. Batch BO then puts the next build's settings where the model is least sure.
